speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These symptoms suggest a serious underlying condition; to begin our investigation, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or stool color regarding your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The weight loss is significant at twelve pounds; have you noticed any blood in your stool or black, tarry stools? Additionally, have you experienced any recent fevers or a persistent cough?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (specifically Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma or Hodgkin Lymphoma)
The combination of B-symptoms (fevers, night sweats, weight loss), abdominal pain, and a fixed, painless supraclavicular mass is highly suspicious for a malignancy of the lymphatic system. I am requesting a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis and a biopsy of the lymph node to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis
REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy
